Chapter 4: God’s Presence in the Middle of Brokenness.
You know, brokenness is just something we all face, sooner or later. It can show up as loss, disappointment, failure—or maybe it’s just the slow fading of dreams we once held tight.
Most of us try to hide those broken places. We’re afraid people will turn away if they see the cracks. But, what if those are the exact spots where something extraordinary can happen? Time and time again, stories of miracles remind us: the most profound encounters often happen right in the heart of our brokenness.
Picture this: one evening, there’s a man whose life has unraveled. He’s alone, scared, and weighed down by mistakes and regrets. He wonders if hope has run out for him. But instead of finding emptiness, he senses a presence that doesn’t back away—instead, it comes closer. The real miracle here isn’t that his past disappears. It’s the deep reassurance that he’s not beyond reach, no matter how lost he feels.
Then there’s another story—a woman grieving her child. She’s met not with empty words, but with real compassion. No one tries to fix or minimize her pain. Instead, it’s honored. And in that quiet space, healing starts. The miracle isn’t that her loss is undone, but that she’s comforted—truly seen and understood.
Isn’t it true that most of us try to patch ourselves up before asking for help? We get the idea that only the strong, only the worthy deserve attention. But these stories flip that idea upside down. They show us that brokenness isn’t a barrier to love. In fact, it’s often the very place where love shows up most powerfully.
It becomes clear—God’s presence isn’t just for the highlight reels, the victories, or the moments when we’ve got it all together. It’s right there in the quiet, hidden places where pain and hope sit side by side. Those stones of shame, regret, or fear—they might seem unmovable. But they’re no match for a love that never gives up.
Walking through brokenness isn’t easy. Some days, the weight just feels too much, and the way ahead is foggy at best. Yet, even then, there’s this quiet assurance: you’re not alone. The same presence that moved through ancient stories is still here, still bringing hope into the places that need it most.
